The Federal Aviation Administration and the Department of War signed a safety agreement for the southern border and completed a safety assessment of a high-energy laser counter-drone system, validating that the technology poses no undue risk to passenger aircraft [FAA and Department of War Sign Landmark Safety Agreement Protecting the Southern Border](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-and-dow-sign-landmark-safety-agreement-protect-southern-border). This regulatory clearance enables the deployment of directed-energy defenses in protected airspace. Concurrently, the FAA marked a major milestone in the eVTOL Integration Pilot Program as BETA Technologies and United Therapeutics completed a flight test moving organs from Virginia to Maryland in an eVTOL aircraft [FAA Marks Major eVTOL Milestone as Organ Medical Transport Flies Virginia to Maryland](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-announces-major-milestone-evtol-technology-use). The agency also unveiled eight selections for pilot programs testing next-generation aircraft for personal travel, cargo, and emergency medicine, signaling accelerated integration of advanced air mobility into commercial service.

Infrastructure investment supports these operational advances. The Department of Transportation and FAA broke ground on a new advanced air mobility research facility at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center in Oklahoma City to support testing and training of eVTOL aircraft [DOT and FAA Break Ground on New Facility to Support Advanced Air Mobility Research](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/dot-and-faa-break-ground-new-facility-support-advanced-air-mobility-research). Additionally, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced $84.4 million in Airport Improvement Program grants for Texas, North Carolina, and Wyoming to modernize regional airports supporting passenger and cargo operations [FAA Invests $84.4 Million in Airport Improvements in Texas, North Carolina, and Wyoming](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-844-million-airport-improvements). These capital injections aim to strengthen the physical infrastructure required for increased air traffic density.

Workforce expansion remains a critical priority for aviation safety. The FAA hired 2,235 air traffic controller trainees, exceeding its Fiscal Year 2026 goal and setting an all-time record for the agency [FAA Sets All-Time Record for Air Traffic Controller Trainee Hiring](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-breaks-all-time-record-air-traffic-controller-trainee-hiring). To sustain this pipeline, the FAA partnered with Shenandoah University in Virginia and Angelo State University in Texas, the first state colleges to join the Enhanced Air Traffic-Collegiate Training Initiative [First Virginia College Joins FAA Air Traffic Controller Training Program](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-first-virginia-college-join-air). These partnerships expand the candidate pool for certified air traffic control positions.

In autonomous ground transportation, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is moving to permit driverless trucks to use cab-mounted warning beacons instead of traditional hazard triangles, modernizing federal safety requirements [FMCSA Permits Driverless Trucks to Swap Warning Triangles for Cab-Mounted Beacons](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNQlVRTk1zNHRWQnNXcm1RV2Y2Q1VIR212OXJxaUVVb1oxQWxpUjY1WVhiMHhMZzVrSml2TGdVQVN5a3czLUpmNDZZUEY4cEkxTUFmMktBSUppQUNxNkpRcUYwa1VEdmF3NzROR0J2dmdXdGM4QS0ySjg1dTZONFdqOEtIc2NndGU2cjNtWTVlNDlTX3VoZXkwelRYdU43dlk2WGFpRy13NU0wSXA5LUctZDM5ZTlDRjFr). Meanwhile, Charger Logistics signed a deal with Kodiak Robotics to provide autonomous freight-hauling services, expanding real-world commercial use of driverless trucks on freight corridors [Charger Logistics Inks Deal with Kodiak for Autonomous Hauls](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxPSW1EOTFJTkZnWDJveV9DZ0Z2WGNRbHpDUWQweHJOcG9GdERiMmFCQ1Bhb1VEcmFWLUZVZWdwMUR5MjN6MDJyRHVpZjhQZDJQbXRneEJ5TGFlb3lNZW94blQyaXpxa1RGbVlSTE14ZklsdUQ2X3dZUDVUMUVhYXJvby1LRG5YYmhpaVRaOGR1ZW9maWJNdHdmbExpb0NuUU4xc1ptQnBJZzB4Zm1XZkRCdlhSdDViaDdLTmJrU1huO).
